describes: producer 1 of null: the summary read stops swallowing its failure, so a rejected boot read rejects the Promise.all and takes the whole boot down instead of degrading

producer 1 answers an EMPTY RESULT instead of a failure: a sidebar that failed to load is now indistinguishable from an account with no sessions. This is `d80db401` item 2's shape -- a partial failure landing in a value with no field to hold it -- moved from dash's fan-out into this one
producer 2 of null: the recent-bundle read stops swallowing its failure, so one failed bundle fetch rejects boot for every session rather than leaving the turns unhydrated

producer 3 of null: the validator read stops swallowing its failure. Unlike the others this one has a sibling producing the same null on the empty-id branch, so a caller that cannot tell them apart is the thing at risk

producer 3 confused with its sibling: a FAILED validator read now answers exactly what `no cached ids` answers, so a cache that could not be revalidated is treated as a cache with nothing to revalidate
expected_unnoticed: no request is made either way and the value is discarded, so nothing downstream can see it -- measured on both halves. `ApiClient.getValidators` short-circuits an empty id list to `Promise.resolve({})` BEFORE building a url (ApiClient.ts:429), so the mutated empty-ids branch issues no HTTP call and the url recorder cannot separate them. And `validatorsP` is consumed only by `await Promise.all([...])` with the result discarded, so `{}` and `null` reach no consumer at all. P3-validators-catch-A is what pins this read -- it fails the boot when the request rejects, and 'does issue the validator read when there ARE cached ids' pins that the branch is reachable. This declaration goes stale the moment `getValidators` stops short-circuiting an empty list, or `Promise.all`'s result is destructured and the validator value read.

describes: producer 4 of null: the folder read stops swallowing its failure. The comment above it states the intended degradation -- `A failure leaves folders empty, which grouping already treats as not loaded` -- so this mutation asks whether that stated contract is pinned anywhere

producer 4 writes an empty folder list on failure instead of leaving it unset: grouping can no longer tell `folders never loaded` from `this account has no folders`, and the degradation the comment promises is exactly what stops happening
